::: {#rem-counting-depth}

#### Counting depth, and other names

These notes count a network's [depth](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html#def-depth) as lds does,
by its layers of weights,
so AlexNet (@exm-deep-learning) has depth 8.
Other sources count only the hidden layers,
or every layer including the input,
and Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville measure depth as the longest path through the model's computational graph,
noting that there is no single correct way to count it
[@goodfellow2016deep, Ch. 1].
"How deep is deep" has no agreed cutoff either.

[Deep learning](#def-deep-learning) models are almost all
[neural networks](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/neural-nets.html),
also called artificial neural networks,
and a neural network with many layers is called a deep neural network.
The name comes from early models of neurons,
but the networks in these notes are not models of the brain.

:::
